questions.q: What origin did sugar have before becoming cheap and common?
a: Luxury item for elites like the King of Spain
questions.why: Text says sugar was a luxury for privileged people such as the King of Spain.

questions.q: What misconception about calories does the sugar industry exploit?
a: All calories are equal regardless of source
questions.why: The book notes the industry spread the idea that calories are the same no matter their origin.

questions.q: What physiological response to sugar leads to fat storage?
questions.why: Scientists found that eating sugar triggers insulin, causing fat cells to store energy.

questions.q: When did public awareness of sugar's health risks notably rise?
a: After 1960 as heart disease rates climbed
questions.why: The text states people began acknowledging sugar's harm after 1960 when heart disease increased.

questions.q: What organization in 1928 promoted sugar as healthy?
questions.why: The Sugar Institute, created in 1928, ran a campaign presenting sugar as healthy.
